singular VERSION (commit unknown)

Usage: singular wallet address [--config FILE] --vault FILE --network-magic N
       [--passphrase-fd N] [--trace LEVEL] [--trace-to SINK] [--trace-format
       FORMAT]

Print the address of a vault's key

Opens the vault and prints the same address wallet create printed for the same
network. The passphrase is asked once at the terminal, or read from
--passphrase-fd or, on a development network, from SINGULAR_PASSPHRASE.

Available settings:
  Show this help text
  switch: -h|--help

  A JSON file giving the settings the command line and the environment leave
  out.
  option: --config FILE
  env: SINGULAR_CONFIG FILE
  default: singular.json in the working directory, if there is one

  The vault to open.
  option: --vault FILE
  env: SINGULAR_VAULT FILE
  config:
    vault: # or null
      <string>

  The network the address is built for.
  option: --network-magic N

  Read the vault passphrase, one line, from this inherited file descriptor; it
  wins over SINGULAR_PASSPHRASE.
  option: --passphrase-fd N
  default: SINGULAR_PASSPHRASE on a development network, else ask on the
  terminal with the echo off

  How much to narrate: off, what (protocol steps) or how (also their
  mechanics).
  option: --trace LEVEL
  env: SINGULAR_TRACE LEVEL
  config:
    trace: # or null
      <string>
  default: what on a terminal, otherwise off

  Where the narration goes: stderr or file:PATH; repeat for several.
  option: --trace-to SINK
  env: SINGULAR_TRACE_TO SINK
  config:
    trace-to: # or null
      <string>
  default: stderr

  The format of the narration: text for a person, json for a program.
  option: --trace-format FORMAT
  env: SINGULAR_TRACE_FORMAT FORMAT
  config:
    trace-format: # or null
      <string>
  default: text on standard error, json in a file

Where settings come from:
  A setting with an env and a config line above is given in any of three ways,
  and the first that is present wins: the flag, then the variable, then the
  key in the config file, then the default.

  The file is one JSON object whose keys are the setting names without their
  dashes, text or numbers, for example

    {"koios-url": "https://preprod.koios.rest/api/v1", "network-magic": 1}

  It is singular.json in the working directory, or the file named by --config
  or SINGULAR_CONFIG. A path in it means what it means on the command line,
  from where the command runs. A passphrase is never read from the file; the
  environment gives one only on a development network, as SINGULAR_PASSPHRASE.

Environment:
  SINGULAR_LOG         A file the protocol phases are appended to, one line
                       each.
  SINGULAR_PASSPHRASE  The vault passphrase, for a development network only: a
                       command on mainnet (764824073), preprod (1) or preview
                       (2) refuses it. --passphrase-fd wins over it, and a
                       value that is empty is refused.

Example:
  singular wallet address --vault alice.vault --network-magic 1

Output and exit status:
  Prints the address on one line of standard output.
  Exit status 0 on success, 1 when the vault could not be opened, 2 for a
  command line it refused.
